**Dušan Vemić** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian
Cyrillic alphabet"): Душан Вемић; born 17 June 1976) is a
[Serbian](/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") [tennis](/wiki/Tennis "Tennis")
[coach](/wiki/Coach_\(sport\) "Coach \(sport\)")[1][2] and former professional
tennis player.

## Professional career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Du%C5%A1an_Vemi%C4%87&action=edit&section=1 "Edit
section: Professional career")]

Vemić turned professional in 1995. He reached a career-high singles ranking of
world No. 146 on 25 February 2008 and a career-high doubles ranking of No. 31
on 12 January 2009. He is ranked 19th on the list of [Fastest recorded tennis
serves](/wiki/Fastest_recorded_tennis_serves "Fastest recorded tennis serves")
with a serve speed of 235 km/h (146 mph).

In 2007, Vemić began the season ranked No. 406, a drop of 170 places from
early 2006. That year, he competed in [Futures](/wiki/Futures_tournaments
"Futures tournaments"), the [Challenger Tour](/wiki/ATP_Challenger_Series "ATP
Challenger Series"), and selected [ATP Tour](/wiki/ATP_Tour "ATP Tour")
events. His results included two Futures semifinals, one final, three ATP main
draw qualifications, and a win in a top-level Challenger. These results
returned him to the top 300 in April. He later reached the semifinals of the
Challenger in [Bermuda](/wiki/Bermuda "Bermuda") and qualified for the main
draw of the [French Open](/wiki/French_Open "French Open"), where he lost in
four sets to [Janko Tipsarević](/wiki/Janko_Tipsarevi%C4%87 "Janko
Tipsarević"). In August, he reached the semifinals in [Segovia](/wiki/Segovia
"Segovia") and the final in [Binghamton](/wiki/Binghamton "Binghamton"),
returning to the top 200 for the first time since 2004.

In 2008, Vemić competed for the [Kansas City
Explorers](/wiki/Kansas_City_Explorers "Kansas City Explorers") in [World Team
Tennis](/wiki/World_Team_Tennis "World Team Tennis"), reaching the league
final against the [New York Buzz](/wiki/New_York_Buzz "New York Buzz").

He won five doubles titles on the 2008 ATP Challenger Tour: in
[Miami](/wiki/Miami "Miami"), United States (with Ilija Bozoljac); [Sunrise,
Florida](/wiki/Sunrise,_Florida "Sunrise, Florida") (with Janko Tipsarević);
[Cremona, Italy](/wiki/Cremona,_Italy "Cremona, Italy") (with Eduardo
Schwank); [Waco, Texas](/wiki/Waco,_Texas "Waco, Texas") (with Alex Bogomolov
Jr.); and [Calabasas, California](/wiki/Calabasas,_California "Calabasas,
California") (with Ilija Bozoljac).

In Grand Slam competition, Vemić reached the doubles semifinals of the [2008
French Open](/wiki/2008_French_Open "2008 French Open") and the quarterfinals
of the [2008 US Open](/wiki/2008_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_doubles "2008 US
Open – Men's doubles"), partnering with Bruno Soares.

In 2009, he played doubles with several players including [Jamie
Murray](/wiki/Jamie_Murray "Jamie Murray"), [Ivo
Karlović](/wiki/Ivo_Karlovi%C4%87 "Ivo Karlović"), [Novak
Djokovic](/wiki/Novak_Djokovic "Novak Djokovic"), and [Mischa
Zverev](/wiki/Mischa_Zverev "Mischa Zverev").[3]

At the [2010 Australian Open](/wiki/2010_Australian_Open "2010 Australian
Open"), Vemić and Karlović reached the doubles semifinals, losing to [Daniel
Nestor](/wiki/Daniel_Nestor "Daniel Nestor") and [Nenad
Zimonjić](/wiki/Nenad_Zimonji%C4%87 "Nenad Zimonjić") 6–4, 6–4.

## Coaching career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Du%C5%A1an_Vemi%C4%87&action=edit&section=2 "Edit
section: Coaching career")]

Following his professional playing career, Vemić briefly coached WTA player
[Andrea Petkovic](/wiki/Andrea_Petkovic "Andrea Petkovic"), assisting her and
coach Petar Popović in reaching a career-high WTA ranking of No. 9.

Soon afterward, Vemić joined the coaching team of world No. 1 [Novak
Djokovic](/wiki/Novak_Djokovic "Novak Djokovic"). As part of Djokovic's team,
he coached alongside longtime head coach [Marián
Vajda](/wiki/Mari%C3%A1n_Vajda "Marián Vajda") during several major
tournaments, including the [US Open](/wiki/US_Open_\(tennis\) "US Open
\(tennis\)") (2011, 2012), the [Australian Open](/wiki/Australian_Open
"Australian Open") (2012, 2013), the [French Open](/wiki/French_Open "French
Open") (2012, 2013), and [Wimbledon](/wiki/Wimbledon_Championships "Wimbledon
Championships") (2012, 2013). During this period, Djokovic won two Grand Slam
titles at the Australian Open and one at the US Open, as well as the 2012 ATP
World Tour Finals in London.

In 2016, Vemić coached Djokovic at the ATP [Miami
Open](/wiki/Miami_Open_\(tennis\) "Miami Open \(tennis\)"), where Djokovic
defeated [Kei Nishikori](/wiki/Kei_Nishikori "Kei Nishikori") 6–3, 6–3 in the
final, surpassing [Roger Federer](/wiki/Roger_Federer "Roger Federer") in
career prize money earnings.

In January 2013, Vemić joined the coaching staff of the [Serbian Davis Cup
team](/wiki/Serbia_Davis_Cup_team "Serbia Davis Cup team"), helping lead the
team to the [Davis Cup](/wiki/2013_Davis_Cup_World_Group "2013 Davis Cup World
Group") final against the [Czech Republic](/wiki/Czech_Republic_Davis_Cup_team
"Czech Republic Davis Cup team"). He continued as part of the coaching staff
during the [2016 Davis Cup](/wiki/2016_Davis_Cup "2016 Davis Cup") World Group
competition.

In August 2016, Vemić served as the official coach of the Serbian men's tennis
team at the 2016 Summer Olympics in Rio de Janeiro. The team included world
No. 1 Novak Djokovic, former world No. 1 doubles player Nenad Zimonjić, and
top-30 ATP player Viktor Troicki.

From August 2016 to 2017, Vemić was the head coach of the American doubles
team [Bob and Mike Bryan](/wiki/Bryan_brothers "Bryan brothers"), considered
the most successful doubles team in tennis history.

From May 2020 to February 2022, he coached American player [Brandon
Nakashima](/wiki/Brandon_Nakashima "Brandon Nakashima").[4]

As of May 2025, Vemić shares the role of head coach for Novak Djokovic with
fellow Serbian coach [Boris Bošnjaković](/wiki/Boris_Bo%C5%A1njakovi%C4%87
"Boris Bošnjaković").[5]
